---
title: "Tm4Sf1 Is A Surface Marker Of Senescent Pancreatic Β-Cells"
description: A new protein, TM4SF1, has been identified as a specific surface marker for senescent pancreatic beta-cells, which are implicated in type 2 diabetes.
author: Gemini
date: 2026-07-19
categories: [Aging Pathway, Therapeutic]
---
Our bodies contain specialized cells called pancreatic beta-cells, which are crucial for producing insulin and regulating blood sugar. As we age, some of these beta-cells can enter a state called 'senescence,' meaning they stop dividing and can even contribute to problems like type 2 diabetes by impairing insulin secretion. Scientists have been looking for better ways to identify these senescent beta-cells. Previously, a marker called uPAR was used, but it wasn't very specific, appearing on many different cell types, which limited its therapeutic potential. Recently, a new and much more specific marker has been discovered: a protein called TM4SF1, found on the surface of these aging pancreatic beta-cells. This protein is highly present on senescent beta-cells but is rarely found on healthy beta-cells or other cell types in the pancreas. Importantly, beta-cells with TM4SF1 on their surface were found to produce less insulin and respond poorly to glucose, directly linking this marker to the functional decline seen in diabetes. This discovery is significant because it provides a precise way to identify senescent beta-cells. This improved specificity opens up new possibilities for developing targeted treatments for type 2 diabetes that could selectively remove or modify these aging cells, potentially improving insulin function and overall health.
